title: Giant covalent structures; States of matter and phase changes
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD08#t1 term and clue written for the game; BD08#t3 term and clue written for the game; BD05#t4 term and clue written for the game; BD05#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BD05#N.7, BD08#N.2a, BD05#N.11a, BD08#N.8a, BD08#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Sublimation
items.clue: Change of state directly from solid to gas.

items.label: Evaporation
items.clue: Liquid turns to gas at the surface only, at any temperature.

items.label: Fullerenes
items.clue: Closed cages of C atoms, such as C₆₀, that exist as separate molecules.

items.label: Graphene
items.clue: A single sheet one atom thick that conducts and is very strong for its mass.

questions.stem: Substance X melts at 1710 °C. It does not conduct electricity, either as a solid or when molten. It does not dissolve in water or in hexane. Which structure does X have?

options.text: A lattice of oppositely charged ions
A network of atoms joined by covalent bonds throughout
A lattice of metal cations in a sea of delocalised electrons
Separate small molecules with very strong forces between them

questions.explanation: The very high melting point means strong bonds break. No conduction even when molten means no ions and no delocalised electrons. Insoluble everywhere: a covalent network.

questions.stem: Which substance is a compound, and for the correct reason?

options.text: Oxygen, since each of its molecules contains two atoms bonded together
Air, since it contains several elements in the same proportions everywhere
Carbon dioxide, since it contains atoms of two elements bonded in a fixed ratio
Salt water, since the salt and the water have combined to form one new substance

questions.explanation: CO₂ contains carbon and oxygen atoms bonded in a fixed 1 : 2 ratio: a compound.

questions.stem: Graphite conducts electricity far better along its layers than at right angles to them. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Its layers slide over each other, and charge is carried only in the direction they slide.
Its ions lie between the layers, so they can move only in the plane of the layers.
Each atom forms four bonds within its layer, so no electrons are left to pass between layers.
Its delocalised electrons move freely within a layer, but cannot easily cross the gap to the next.

questions.explanation: Each C bonds to three others; its fourth electron is delocalised over its own layer only. So charge flows easily along a layer, but hardly between layers.

questions.stem: A molecular solid, X, is heated at a constant rate. Its temperature rises to 80 °C, stays at 80 °C for six minutes while the solid melts, and then rises again. Which explains why the temperature stays constant while X melts?

options.text: The energy supplied is lost to the surroundings, so X absorbs none of it as it melts
The energy absorbed overcomes attractions between molecules; their average Ek is constant
The energy absorbed breaks the covalent bonds within each of the molecules of X
The energy absorbed is used to make each molecule expand as the solid melts

questions.explanation: Temperature measures average kinetic energy. While X melts, the energy separates molecules against their attractions, so the temperature stays constant.

questions.stem: A drop of steam at 100 °C on the skin causes a far worse burn than a drop of the same mass of water at 100 °C. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Steam molecules at 100 °C have a higher average kinetic energy than water molecules at 100 °C.
Steam releases its enthalpy of vaporisation as it condenses on the skin, then cools like the water.
Steam contains hydrogen and oxygen, which react on the skin and release energy.
Steam is a gas, so each gram of it stores more energy per degree than liquid water does.

questions.explanation: 18 g of steam releases about 41 kJ just by condensing. Cooling 18 g of water from 100 °C to 37 °C releases only about 5 kJ more.
